convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I stole from someone who trusted me. I think about it every day."
Aki has an edge today — something curdled.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on their secret."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
You show them Hickory Nuts — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask? I mean it."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "George always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Sleep's gone strange. I memorize the stars at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Okay, that's my quota of socializing."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"What's something from your old life that's actually useful here?"
"Mm. Not dumb at all. The people who can't wait are the ones who make mistakes. You're an asset."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Being a rail conductor taught me to read people fast — who's lying, who's scared, who needs a job. Turns out that's a survival skill. Who knew."
"Still on your useful old-life skills."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Just... be straight with me."
"George is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Hickory Nuts — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I keep turning over the last thing George said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"We're done for now. Not done-done. For now."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"My wound needs a second pair of hands. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"I dreamed George was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
You show them Hickory Nuts — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"And... scene. Good talk."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" Aki sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Aki digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1804 kcal to the pantry.)
"I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us? Seen worse."
"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Still on what you think happened to us."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Don't make me repeat it."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "George owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
It's quiet at the cache spot. Miriam doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Go. But sit with what I said."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Has this changed you? Like, fundamentally?"
"The old you got you here. The new you keeps you here. Both count."
Whatever warmth was building cools to politeness.
"Still on how this changed you."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The sickness took Linh. I keep washing my hands like it'll bring them back. Stupid."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Hah. Every laugh out there feels wrong today. Then I feel wrong for thinking it."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
You walk to the tree line with Liam. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I got lost in it for a second. What did you want to ask?"
"Linh owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"I check everyone's shoes for wear. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Nobody says Linh's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Still on what's been happening. Not that it matters."
You show them Hickory Nuts — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I don't know what to do with my hands today. Anyway."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
Leonor shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Oh — Heh. Nobody's asked me that in a while. ...I'm alright. Getting there."
"Since Linh died... I keep expecting to see Linh at the fire. Stupid."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"You said something took us. Something big. I keep watching the sky since you said it."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
"Here. I made an extra." Aki presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"Still on that personal stuff."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Since Khaled died... I keep expecting to see Khaled at the fire. Stupid."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Right. Go on, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I saw something in the woods I'm not telling anyone about. Worth considering."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on their secret. You'd know about that."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
You show them Chickweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Khaled is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
Aki: "Don't just stand there — you've got opinions, right?"
"This wound — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
You spend time tending them. This was care, not a promise of a cure.
"Still on that favor."
"I've got things to do. People to avoid. You know."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Come forage with me tomorrow — two of us can fill packs."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the east treeline in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
You show them Taro — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

deathBeat: d20: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. George Miller is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d20: 🕯️ George Miller is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d20: The village's quarrel was with George — and George is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
recoverHome: d21: That night, they bring George home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d20: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d20: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."

d20: ◈ ARC III — ENGINES. SYSTEM: "VIEWERSHIP MILESTONE. Organic unit demonstrates compounding capability. Resonance protocols unlocked." — Your gifts deepen. Used in sequence, they resonate. The village is no longer just surviving. It is becoming something.
burialWindowSay: d20: The village's quarrel was with George — and George is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d21: That night, they bring George home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d22: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+6 integration)
d23: You say a few words for George. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d23: You bury George. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
echoSample: d23: "Huh. Let me think about that." "George always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
d23: "George is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
d23: "I keep turning over the last thing George said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
d23: "I dreamed George was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
d27: "You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "George owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
echoV2Sample: d23: The village raises a marker by the fire — George, day 23. the wild. A place to stand.
echoV2DeltaSample: d23: The village raises a marker by the fire — George, day 23. the wild. A place to stand.
halfRationLines: d28: "Triage tents and broth for the sick, or half rations till it passes, or the healthy hunt hard to keep everyone fed. Pick — everything costs."

lastSay: d65: (Relief is open — triage, rations, hunt, or rally, from the beats row. Each option works once; the moment passes in ~3 days.)
d66: — DAY 66 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
d66: Overnight, Purslane; Cattail went bad — beyond saving. You leave them for the flies.
d66: Fresh food keeps days, not weeks. Smoke it over a fire to make it last.
d66: Dawn. You wake rested. (+0 health, energy restored. By the fire. Good enough.)
